conviction_note: Macau and Singapore data for Q3 lean negative against a ~$0.75-0.77 EPS bar (Q3 2025 printed $0.78), but the stock is already down ~19% since the Q2 print and sits 4.6% above its 52-week low. Calls are bid (25d skew -10.7, put/call OI 0.53), short interest is moderate-to-elevated, and the buyback runs at low prices. So the findings net to about +0.2 and the scaled number is slightly negative: p_up 48 on a 7.0% absolute move, set above the 5.55% implied because the name's median reaction is 8.6% and VIP hold makes the Macau line two-sided. The two measures differ in sign only by noise. Both say no edge.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS ~$0.75-0.77, revenue ~$3.40bn. Sources: the sweep row's 'already_in_the_wire' ($0.75 / $3.40bn); Metirai, $0.77 over 8 estimates, range $0.72-0.85 (https://www.metirai.com/finance/LVS/earnings); Zacks Research cut its Q3 to $0.77 from $0.79 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/q3-eps-estimates-for-las-vegas-sands-cut-by-zacks-research-2026-08-06/). The EPS sources roughly agree. Revenue has one source. The company gives no quantitative guidance (Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001300514/000130051426000078/lvs_ex991x06302026.htm). Prior-year compare, Q3 2025: adj EPS $0.78, Macao EBITDA $601m, MBS EBITDA $743m incl. +$43m hold, consolidated $1.34bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1300514/000130051425000157/lvs_ex991x09302025.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest 17.8M shares at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement, days to cover 4.59 (curvedtrading via search snippet: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lvs/short-interest/; fetch returned 403, so snippet_only). That is about 6.8% of the ~261M non-Adelson float: 647.7M shares outstanding and a 59.7% Adelson/Chafetz group per the 13D/A of 2026-08-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1300514/000119312526345232/primary_doc.xml). Benzinga showed 12.7% of float short and rising as of 2026-07-31 (https://jp.benzinga.com/quote/LVS/sentiment). No October settlement found. Skew from the baseline: 25d IV(put)-IV(call) is -10.7 vol points, so upside is paid. Put/call OI 0.53. Event-implied move 5.55% (aggregator ±6.0-6.5%). Tape: spot $37.44, -46% from the 52-week high, +4.6% from the 52-week low, 20d -4.5%. The stock was ~$46 after the Q2 print in late July, so it has already de-rated about 19% on the weak Aug/Sep Macau prints. Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

findings.finding: Macau market GGR fell 3.7-3.8% YoY in Q3 2026: July MOP20.3bn (-8.4%), August MOP21.89bn (-1.2%), September MOP18.06bn (-1.2%), against September forecasts of up to +10-12% that brokers cut before the release. Seaport's 2026-10-20 preview puts Q3 market EBITDA at -10.6% YoY. Applied to LVS's Q3 2025 Macao EBITDA of $601m, that gives roughly $535-540m, before any share loss. An EPS bar of $0.75-0.77, flat to Q3 2025's $0.78, leans on a lower share count and a normal Macau hold to get there.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Macau margin was the line in Apr-2026 (Q1 beat, stock -8.6% on Macau margin and reinvestment) and Jan-2026 (beat, -14.0% on Sands China net income). In Jul-2026 Macau EBITDA missed on low VIP hold ($430m vs $517m hold-normalised) and the stock rose +1.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The monthly GGR is public and the stock fell from ~$46 to ~$37 as August and September missed. What may not be fully priced is how the -10.6% market EBITDA estimate (published only yesterday) maps onto Sands China's higher-opex, VIP-heavy mix. If it were fully priced, consensus EPS would sit below the prior year's $0.78 by more than the share-count effect.
findings.independence: Seaport 3Q26 preview via snippet (https://asgam.com/2026/10/20/seaport-macau-earnings-season-to-highlight-tough-3q26-operating-environment-before-headwinds-comps-ease-in-coming-quarters/, fetch 403). July figure from https://cdcgaming.com/brief/macau-ggr-down-8-4-year-on-year-to-us2-51-billion-in-july/. Those are three outlets for one DICJ series, so they count as one fact.

findings.finding: Sands China was losing share going into Q3. J.P. Morgan (2026-08-26) put its Q2 GGR share at 24%, down 2 points QoQ, with hold-adjusted EBITDA share at a new low of 27% (-220bp). The Venetian fell to 7.6% while Wynn gained 120bp. Management had said opex growth would slow in H2 2026 and that 400-500 Venetian rooms stay out of inventory each quarter into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan-2026 and Apr-2026 prints were sold 14.0% and 8.6% on Macau share/margin quality despite headline beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 share data is public. Whether the slide continued in Q3, with Wynn and MGM yet to report, is not visible to anyone until tonight. If the market were already pricing a further share loss, consensus Macau EBITDA would sit below the market-wide -10.6%, and there is no sign it does.
findings.independence: The opex and rooms commentary is from a different document, the Q2 call (https://agbrief.com/news/macau/23/07/2026/sands-china-keeps-700m-macau-ebitda-target-as-vip-share-rises/). CreditSights (April) expected share gains but lower margins (https://asgam.com/2026/04/27/creditsights-sands-chinas-market-share-to-keep-growing-in-2026-but-margins-to-trend-lower/).

findings.finding: Singapore visitor arrivals were soft through Q3: August 1.61m (-0.3% YoY), September 1.23m (-2.2% YoY), January-September -1.7%. Mainland Chinese arrivals were up 4.8% YTD. MBS hold-normalised EBITDA was $652m in Q2 2026 against about $688m in Q2 2025 (-5%), and JPM's Q2 MBS estimate of $727m was missed at $689m. Against Q3 2025's $743m reported (about $700m hold-normalised), a flat-to-down MBS is the likely base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MBS has been the offset. In Oct-2025 (+12.4%) MBS EBITDA was $743m, +83% YoY, and the CEO raised the property's outlook.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (STB September data; month inferred from content)
findings.why_not_priced: Tourism arrivals are a weak proxy for MBS's ultra-premium mass and VIP book, which nobody aggregates. Because of that the market may still anchor MBS on the Q1 $788m. If it had priced the softness, MBS estimates would sit near Q2's $652m hold-normalised level.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The MBS numbers come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001300514/000130051426000078/lvs_ex991x06302026.htm), and the JPM Q2 estimate from https://www.ggrasia.com/?p=192172 via snippet. The China +4.8% YTD figure cuts slightly the other way.

findings.finding: VIP rolling hold is a large two-sided swing factor this quarter. In Q2, Macau rolling hold was 1.35% against 3.3% expected, which cost $87m of EBITDA, 'the largest hold adjustment we've ever had'. Rolling volume rose 73% YoY and Sands China is now #1 in VIP with a 26% volume share, so EBITDA variance from hold is higher than at any time since reopening. Consensus presumably assumes normal hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul-2026: reported EBITDA was depressed by low hold and the stock rose +1.7% as investors looked through it. The market does look through hold when it is disclosed.
findings.why_not_priced: Sign unknowable, so it adds no direction. It raises the absolute move and is carried in abs_move_pct, not in the sign.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K Exhibit 5 hold-adjustment table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001300514/000130051426000078/lvs_ex991x06302026.htm). Same company source.

findings.finding: Capital return at depressed prices. On 2026-07-21 the board reset the repurchase authorization to $6.0bn through July 2029, after $787m was bought in Q2 at an average $52.37. Q3 traded at about $37-46, so each dollar retires roughly 20% more shares. On 2026-09-01, LVS's subsidiary bought Sands China shares on market to take its stake to 75.01%, and Sands China moved to HKEX's alternative public-float test, which leaves room to keep buying. Unrestricted cash was $3.38bn, plus $4.26bn of revolver.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback has not prevented sell-offs on weak Macau prints (Jan, Apr 2026). The $6bn reset came with the Jul-2026 print, which closed +1.7% after an after-hours drop of about 6.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. The Q3 repurchase dollars and the share count are not, and a large quarterly buyback at ~$40 lifts per-share numbers and signals management's view. Had it been priced, the stock would not be trading at the 52-week low with a Zacks #5.
findings.independence: Sands China stake purchase: https://sigma.world/news/lvs-unit-pushes-sands-china-holding-above-75/. Share count 647.7M from the 13D/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1300514/000119312526345232/primary_doc.xml).

findings.finding: Positioning and expectations are depressed into the print. Spot is $37.44, 4.6% above the 52-week low and about 19% below the post-Q2 level of ~$46. The 25d skew is -10.7 vol points (calls over puts) and put/call OI is 0.53. Short interest was 17.8M shares (~6.8% of non-insider float, DTC ~4.6) in mid-July, and Benzinga flagged it as rising. The shares carry a Zacks #5. The name rallied +1.7% on an outright Q2 miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last 7 prints, 5 were up. Beats were sold (Jan -14.0%, Apr -8.6%) and a miss was bought (Jul +1.7%). From a low base the stock has risen +11 to +12% (Jan-2025, Oct-2025).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is not an information edge. It records that the downside case is visibly paid for: if the market were complacent, the skew would be put-bid and the stock would not be at the bottom of its range.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -10.7 and put/call OI 0.53 (sealed). Short interest from https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/lvs/short-interest/ (snippet) and https://jp.benzinga.com/quote/LVS/sentiment (snippet).

findings.finding: Q4 commentary on the call should read better than Q3. Golden Week 2026 visitor arrivals topped 1 million. Macau's Chief Executive (2026-10-11) kept the MOP240bn full-year GGR forecast, which needs only about MOP16.3bn a month for Oct-Dec. Seaport expects Q4 GGR -0.7% and EBITDA -3.4% YoY as comps ease, against -3.8% and -10.6% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LVS gives no numeric guide. Call commentary on current trends has driven the reaction: Oct-2025 +12.4% on MBS outlook, Jan-2026 -14.0% on Macau.
findings.why_not_priced: No October GGR datapoint is public before November 1, so management's October color on the call is the first company-level read. It is only a proxy now: had a firm October been priced, the stock would have bounced off its low after Golden Week, and it has not (20d -4.5%).
findings.independence: Proxy. The Seaport Q4 estimate (https://asgam.com/2026/10/20/seaport-macau-earnings-season-to-highlight-tough-3q26-operating-environment-before-headwinds-comps-ease-in-coming-quarters/) shares a document with finding 1.

baseline_tension: The fundamental proxies (Macau Q3 -3.8% GGR, -10.6% EBITDA, share loss, soft Singapore arrivals) point down, but the skew (calls bid), the 52-week-low tape and moderate short interest say the market has already paid for that downside. The negatives were shrunk and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign against a strong skew; short interest checked): the Macau GGR finding went from -1.0 to -0.8 and the share-loss finding from -0.7 to -0.5, because the -10.7 call-bid skew and ~6.8-12.7% short float argue the downside is held.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller; a broader series was filed): the Singapore arrivals finding went from -0.6 to -0.3, because the China-arrivals series (+4.8% YTD) and MBS's premium mix weaken the transmission.
Rule 6 (bar): the EPS bar is two-sourced and roughly agreeing ($0.75 / $0.77), so no cap. Revenue is single-sourced, so print_vs_bar_pct is held small.
'Asking what was missed generates pessimism' plus rule 3: p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Rules 1, 2 and 8 changed nothing: no one-off items, the positioning finding already reflects the beats-sold/miss-bought history, and this is not a thin-coverage name.
